$comment: Words that mean the same thing in every industry. Spellings follow OpenID Connect Core 5.1 wherever it has the claim: inventing a second name for birthdate is how two issuers end up unreadable to each other while both being right. Aliases record a spelling that already exists in the wild and what it means, because credentials already issued carry the old key and no later decision can change that.

claims.name: name
claims.meaning: The full name, as the person writes it.

claims.name: birthdate
claims.meaning: The day the person was born.

claims.name: email
claims.meaning: A mailbox the person can be reached at.

claims.name: phone_number
claims.meaning: A telephone number in E.164 form.

claims.name: gender
claims.meaning: Gender as the person states it.

aliases.why: Vaulet's original spelling; OIDC Core says phone_number.
Vaulet's original spelling; OIDC Core says birthdate.
Vaulet's original spelling; OIDC Core's name is the full name.
The MRZ field, not the stated gender — it belongs to the document vocabulary.
